title: UiState
description: Response of `GET /ui/state`: everything the flyout shows, in one poll.

first_session_at_ms.description:
When a Claude session first registered with this install, or `None` when none ever
has, which shows the first-run card.

generated_at_ms.description:
When the state was built, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Elapsed and waited
times are measured against it, so they do not depend on the tray app's clock.

meters.description: Machine meters for the Resources card.

notices.description: Kills and removals, with whether Claude has been told yet.

sessions.description: Every registered session, with or without leases.

ActiveJob.description: An active lease and the process its command runs as.

process.description: The command's process, or `None` when the session has no process to show.

BenchmarkProgress.description: Where a waiting benchmark lease stands, so its holder can report progress.

oneOf.description: Other leases are still active; nothing new starts until they end.
The machine has drained and its background load is being averaged.

cpu_avg_pct.description: Average total CPU load so far, in percent.

gpu_avg_pct.description: Average load of the busiest GPU engine so far, in percent.

oneOf.description:
The average is above the quiet limits. The lease is granted anyway, marked as not
quiet, once `grant_anyway_in_secs` have passed.

cpu_avg_pct.description: Average total CPU load over the quiet window, in percent.

cpu_limit_pct.description: CPU limit of a quiet machine.

gpu_avg_pct.description: Average load of the busiest GPU engine over the quiet window, in percent.

gpu_limit_pct.description: GPU limit of a quiet machine.

grant_anyway_in_secs.description: Seconds until the lease is granted without quiet.

BoundProcess.description: One process, identified across PID reuse.

start_time.description: Start time of `pid` in seconds since the Unix epoch, as in [`Holder::pid_start_time`].

history_pct.description: Recent once-a-second loads for the sparkline, oldest first, at most 24.

reserved_cores.description: Logical cores reserved by active leases.

usage_pct.description: Total load over the last second, as a percentage of all logical processors.

DriveUsage.description: Space and activity of one fixed drive.

name.description: Drive letter with its colon, for example `C:`.

read_bytes_per_sec.description: Bytes read per second over the last second.

write_bytes_per_sec.description: Bytes written per second over the last second.

EndCause.description:
Why a lease ended.

Kept apart from [`LeaseState`], whose values are fixed by the database's CHECK constraints
and by older `rh-mcp` builds that reject unknown states.

oneOf.description: The daemon ended it because the heartbeat stopped or the holder died.
The user stopped the job and its process tree.
The user removed the request from the queue before it started.

busiest_pct.description: Load of the busiest engine group over the last second, in percent.

name.description: Adapter name, for example `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070`.

reserved_pct.description:
Engine load reserved by active leases, in percent. Leases reserve on the adapter with
the most video memory only, so it is 0 on every other adapter.

reserved_vram_mb.description: Video memory reserved by active leases; 0 on every adapter but the reserving one.

vram_total_mb.description: Dedicated video memory installed, when the OS reports it.

config_error.description:
Why the last change to `config.toml` was rejected; the daemon keeps the config it had
until the file is fixed.

Holder.description: The process a session's leases live and die with.

pid.description: PID of the session's `claude.exe`, the direct parent of its MCP server and its hooks.

pid_start_time.description:
Start time of `pid` in seconds since the Unix epoch. Windows reuses PIDs, so a process
with the same PID but another start time is not the holder.

JobClass.description: Named job profiles. Their values come from the `[classes]` section of the config.

oneOf.description: Short jobs that barely load the machine.
Compiles, test suites, and other CPU-bound work.
Training, rendering, games, and other GPU-bound work.
Jobs that load both the CPU and the GPU.

JobProcess.description: The process shown for a job.

bound.description:
Whether this is the root of the command's bound process tree, the only tree a kill
ends. `false` means it is the session's busiest process, shown for display only.

exe.description: Full path of the executable, for its icon; `None` when it could not be read.

JobProfile.description: Resources a job is expected to need while it runs.

cores.description: Logical cores the job keeps busy.

gpu_pct.description: GPU engine load as a percentage of one adapter.

Lease.description: A reservation of machine resources for one job.

binding.description:
The command the lease's holder last reported running under it; `None` until the hook
reports one.

class.description: Class the profile was taken from, or `None` for a custom profile.

cwd.description: Working directory of the command, or empty when the requester did not say.

end_cause.description:
Why the lease ended; `None` while it is queued or active, and for leases that ended
before causes were recorded.

ended_at_ms.description: When the lease was released or expired.

expires_at_ms.description: When the lease expires unless a heartbeat arrives first.

kind.description: How the lease shares the machine.

label.description: What the lease is for, usually the command that will run.

profile.description: Resources reserved while the lease is active.

requested_at_ms.description: When the lease was requested, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

LeaseBinding.description:
The command a lease covers, as the PreToolUse hook reported it, and the process tree it
runs as once that is found. A later report for the same lease replaces it.

bound_at_ms.description:
When the hook reported the command, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Processes
that started before it are never part of the command.

root.description: Root of the command's process tree; `None` until it is found.

tool_use_id.description: Claude Code's ID for the tool call that runs the command.

LeaseId.description: Identifies a lease. Assigned by the daemon's database when the lease is first stored.

LeaseKind.description: How a lease shares the machine.

oneOf.description: Runs alongside other leases as long as their reservations fit.
Runs alone on a quiet machine so that measurements are not disturbed.

LeaseState.description: Where a lease is in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Granted; its reservation counts against the machine.
Ended by the daemon because the heartbeat stopped or the holder died.

Meters.description: Machine meters with the share that leases reserve.

drives.description: Every fixed drive, by drive letter.

headroom_pct.description: Percentage of each resource that leases never take, from `admission.headroom_pct`.

NoiseReport.description:
Load from processes outside the holder's session while a benchmark lease was active.

CPU is the summed per-process load of every other session and of processes outside all
sessions. Kernel and interrupt time belongs to no process, so it is not counted: it would
otherwise charge the benchmark's own system time as noise.

avg_cpu_pct.description: Average CPU load of other processes, as a percentage of all logical processors.

avg_gpu_pct.description: Average GPU engine load of other processes, as a percentage of one adapter.

peak_cpu_pct.description: Peak CPU load of other processes.

peak_gpu_pct.description: Peak GPU engine load of other processes.

quiet_at_start.description:
Whether the machine met the quiet limits when the lease was granted. `false` means it
was granted anyway after the longest quiet wait.

Notice.description: A kill or removal that Claude must hear about once.

command.description: The lease's label, usually the command.

delivered_at_ms.description: When a hook or tool result told the session, or `None` while it has not been told.

ended_at_ms.description: When the lease ended, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

lease_id.description: Lease the notice is about. A lease ends once, so this also identifies the notice.

QueuedJob.description: A queued lease and why it waits.

position.description: Place in the queue, starting at 1.

verdict.description: Why it waits, the expected wait, and benchmark progress when it is a benchmark.

command.description: The lease's label, usually the command as it was run.

end_cause.description: Why it ended; `None` for runs recorded before causes were.

ended_at_ms.description: End of the run, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

lease_id.description: Lease the job ran under, if the lease is still stored.

noise.description: Background load during the run; present only for benchmark leases.

session.description: Session that ran it; `None` for runs recorded before sessions were.

started_at_ms.description: Start of the run, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

ResourceUsage.description: Resources used by a process or a group of processes, in the units of [`JobProfile`].

cores.description: CPU load in logical cores, for example `2.5` for two and a half busy cores.

gpu_pct.description: GPU engine load as a percentage of one adapter.

SessionKey.description:
Identifies a Claude Code session by its `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`.

The MCP server reads the value from its environment and the hook reads `session_id` from
its stdin JSON; both see the same string.

cwd.description:
Working directory of the session's most recent lease, which names its project; `None`
when no lease gave one.

usage.description: Live usage of the session's whole process subtree.

Verdict.description: The admission engine's answer. Response of `POST /can-fit`.

benchmark.description: Where a benchmark at the head of the queue stands; `None` for other requests.

fits.description: Whether the job could start now.

reasons.description: Human-readable explanations, one per limiting or notable factor.

wait_estimate_secs.description: Expected wait before the job fits, when the daemon can estimate it.
